name: DeepSeek-V3 / R1 absorbed MoE decoder · Decode KV 分片
description: Absorbed MLA with BF16 analytical residency and published V3-family routing.

sources.text: Main decoder only, with absorbed MLA and explicit rectangular attention temporaries. BF16 analytical weight residency except the FP32 routing correction; published checkpoint FP8 storage, MTP, speculative decoding, YaRN table creation and kernel fusion are outside this definition.

Routed experts use sigmoid affinities. Group and expert selection use corrected scores; weights come from the original affinities, normalized over selected experts and scaled by 2.5. Comparison counts are analytical proxies. Routed weight traffic uses an upper bound on distinct experts touched per call.

Expert weights are evenly split by striped owner (expert e belongs to rank e mod P). Each token still selects K experts globally. The theoretical route budget distributes those K slots by quotient and remainder. Each owner reserves ceil(K/P) slots; useful work, token gathers and routed weight reads use valid slots, while executed slot work includes padding. Each owner packs its rows from the replicated token, IDs and original normalized scores, and the routed partials are summed before adding replicated shared experts.

Analytical routed-expert TP slices matching gate and up channels and the same down-projection inputs. The packed gate/up activation stores channel pairs together. TP peers in an owner group use the same valid routes, and route-weighted hidden partials can be summed across owners and feature ranks in one reduction before adding replicated shared experts.
Routed matrix traffic uses the fraction of locally resident experts touched by valid routes and includes their per-matrix storage auxiliaries.

Decode reserves contiguous equally sized MLA slots. Each request group merges FP32 score maxima, denominators and latent weighted sums. Each rank scans its reserved slots, masks unused entries and appends the current latent and rotary key only if it owns the slot. The weighted-value multiply rounds unnormalized weights to BF16.
